name: mbedtls

patches.replace: /* #define MBEDTLS_NET_C -- disabled for this port, see mbedtls.json's notes */
patches.reason: library/net_sockets.c's portable (non-_WIN32) path needs a fuller BSD-sockets surface than this PAL currently exposes -- confirmed by a real build attempt, not assumed: select()/fd_set/FD_ZERO/FD_SET/FD_ISSET/suseconds_t/SO_TYPE all came back as undeclared on Windows. This is squarely curl's territory (the next port in this queue, which genuinely needs sockets), not this crypto-only first pass -- mbedtls's own SSL/TLS layer only calls into net_sockets.c through the mbedtls_net_context callback shape a *consumer* can already swap out for its own I/O, so disabling MBEDTLS_NET_C does not block AES/SHA/RSA/etc. use at all, only the convenience BSD-socket helper this port's own test doesn't use.

Windows-only in effect (guarded by CRT_TARGET_OS_WINDOWS, a macro tools/crt-cc itself predefines for Windows targets -- genuine no-op on Linux/macOS, where MBEDTLS_HAVE_ASM stays on as upstream intends). A plain -UMBEDTLS_HAVE_ASM on the Windows CFLAGS (the same technique that works for _WIN32/MBEDTLS_NET_C-adjacent macros elsewhere in this recipe) was tried first and did NOT work -- confirmed by a real build attempt still hitting the same #error -- because, unlike those, mbedtls_config.h's own `#define MBEDTLS_HAVE_ASM` line has no #ifndef guard, so it unconditionally redefines the macro back to defined regardless of the command line. Needed alongside MBEDTLS_HAVE_INT32 below: bignum.h's own check_config.h refuses HAVE_INT32/HAVE_INT64 and HAVE_ASM defined simultaneously.

Windows-only (CRT_TARGET_OS_WINDOWS-guarded, same pattern as MBEDTLS_HAVE_ASM above). AESNI_C's own library/aesni.h hard-#errors unless either compiler intrinsics (needs -maes -mpclmul target flags this recipe doesn't pass) or MBEDTLS_HAVE_ASM (disabled above, for the unrelated bignum __udivti3/compiler-rt gap) are available. Not a correctness loss: aes.c's own portable, table-based C implementation is used instead whenever AESNI_C is off, exactly as on any CPU without real AES-NI hardware -- confirmed correct by this port's own test (a real AES-128-CBC encrypt/decrypt round trip). Revisit if a future pass wants Windows AES-NI acceleration specifically (would need -maes/-mpclmul CFLAGS instead of disabling the feature).

patches.replace:
ifdef WINDOWS_BUILD
# -lbcrypt disabled for this port, see mbedtls.json's notes
endif
patches.reason: Applies to every WINDOWS=1 build (compile AND link, not just the .dll recipes below): mbedtls's Windows entropy source (library/entropy_poll.c's _WIN32 branch) calls BCryptGenRandom, needing a real bcrypt.lib this PAL doesn't provide. Safe to drop: target_overrides.windows.env.CFLAGS already undefines _WIN32 (see that note below), so entropy_poll.c never compiles the BCryptGenRandom branch at all -- it takes the portable getrandom()/fopen("/dev/urandom") path instead, which needs no bcrypt import. First discovered by a real build attempt (`lld: error: unable to find library -lbcrypt`), not assumed in advance -- WINDOWS_BUILD's own -lbcrypt line applies globally regardless of which entropy code path actually got compiled.

libmbedtls.dll's own link recipe (only reached when WINDOWS=1 is passed, see the WINDOWS=1 make_args override below) hardcodes -lws2_32/-lwinmm/-lgdi32 (real Windows SDK import libraries this PAL doesn't provide) and -Wl,-soname (an ELF-only GNU ld concept lld-link's PE frontend doesn't understand) and -static-libgcc (irrelevant to clang/compiler-rt). ws2_32/winmm/gdi32 are safe to drop: MBEDTLS_NET_C (the only thing that would call into winsock) is already disabled by the patch above, and nothing else in this crypto-only build touches multimedia timers (winmm) or GDI. --out-implib is kept -- it is the same GNU-ld-compatible import-library flag this project's own crt-cc/lld-link Windows shared-build path already understands.
Same fix as libmbedtls.dll's recipe above, applied to libmbedx509.dll.
Same fix as libmbedtls.dll's recipe above, applied to libmbedcrypto.dll.

notes: Next in the porting matrix expansion queue after bzip2/xz/pcre2 (see TODO.md's "Porting matrix expansion" bullet). Picked the 3.6.7 LTS release (supported through at least March 2027), not the newer 4.2.0: 4.2.0 dropped the plain top-level Makefile entirely in favor of a CMake-only build, and this project's tooling (tools/crt-port-build.py) has no CMake-driven-port support at all -- 3.6.7 still ships a real, hand-written top-level Makefile.

skip_configure (a new build.system:"configure" flag, added this session to tools/crt-port-build.py's build_configure_port()) -- mbedtls has no ./configure step at all; everything else in the configure-based flow (patches, env/CFLAGS overrides, make_args/install_args, Windows shell wrapping, parallel -jN jobs) is reused unchanged, so this only skips the one step that doesn't apply rather than adding a whole separate 'system' type for one recipe.

install_args (new: a base build.install_args field, distinct from target_overrides.<os>.make_args, extra arguments specific to `make install` only) carries mbedtls's own DESTDIR=@PORT_PREFIX@ install convention -- unlike every other recipe here, mbedtls's Makefile uses `make install DESTDIR=...` (installing straight into DESTDIR, not a staging root prepended to a separate --prefix=), not autotools' --prefix= convention.

make_args: ["lib", "SHARED=1"] targets the top-level Makefile's `lib` goal specifically (`$(MAKE) -C library`), not the default `all` goal (`programs tests`) -- sidesteps the framework/exported.make submodule requirement entirely (the top-level Makefile's own conditional only requires it for goals other than `lib`/`library/%`). SHARED=1 makes library/Makefile's own `all: shared static` build BOTH the static .a and the real shared library in the same invocation (library/Makefile defaults to `static` only when SHARED is unset), so this one recipe covers both static and shared verification together -- see the standing porting-loop discipline item in TODO.md this session added ("verify both the static AND shared build during the same porting pass").

install_args' `-o no_test -o programs -o mbedtls_test` (GNU Make's --old-file/--assume-old option, one per phony prerequisite) routes around a real dependency-chain problem: mbedtls's own `install: no_test` -> `no_test: programs` -> `programs: lib mbedtls_test` chain means a plain `make install` would also try to build every example program under programs/ and the whole mbedtls_test framework (needing framework/exported.make for real this time, and pulling in far more than a library-only port needs). `-o` tells make to treat each of those phony targets as already up to date, so make walks straight to install:'s own recipe body (a handful of mkdir -p/cp -rp/cp -RP commands) without touching its prerequisites at all.

target_overrides.windows.cflags undefines _WIN32/_WIN32_WCE/__WIN32__/WIN32/__MINGW32__ (the same technique as every other Windows recipe here) and additionally defines __unix__: two of mbedtls's own library sources (entropy_poll.c, timing.c) have a HARD #error (not just a silently-empty translation unit) if neither _WIN32 nor a recognized Unix-like macro (unix/__unix/__unix__/__APPLE__+__MACH__/__HAIKU__/__midipix__, see library/common.h's MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_IS_UNIXLIKE derivation) is defined -- since this PAL has no real <windows.h>/<bcrypt.h>/QueryPerformanceCounter to satisfy the _WIN32 branch anyway, -D__unix__ routes them down their portable POSIX branch (getrandom()/fopen("/dev/urandom") for entropy, gettimeofday() for timing) instead.

MBEDTLS_NET_C (networking, on by default) is disabled via the mbedtls_config.h patch: a real Windows build attempt showed this PAL's <sys/socket.h> doesn't yet expose the fuller BSD-sockets surface library/net_sockets.c needs (select()/fd_set/FD_ZERO/FD_SET/FD_ISSET/suseconds_t/SO_TYPE all came back undeclared). Disabling it doesn't block AES/SHA/RSA/etc. use -- mbedtls's SSL/TLS layer only touches net_sockets.c through the mbedtls_net_context callback shape a consumer can already swap for its own I/O. Revisit once curl (the next port in this queue, which genuinely needs sockets) has driven this PAL's socket surface further.

Getting a real, correctly-named Windows shared build (.dll + .dll.a import library, not just a working library) took a chain of real, individually-confirmed fixes, each found by an actual build attempt rather than guessed in advance: (1) library/Makefile's WINDOWS_BUILD-gated -lbcrypt (mbedtls's Windows entropy source calls BCryptGenRandom; unneeded since -D__unix__ above already routes entropy_poll.c off that path) -- patched out. (2) The three .dll link recipes' own -lws2_32/-lwinmm/-lgdi32 (unneeded once MBEDTLS_NET_C is disabled) and their -Wl,-soname (an ELF-only GNU ld concept lld-link's PE frontend doesn't accept) and -static-libgcc -- patched out, keeping --out-implib (the GNU-ld-compatible import-library flag this project's own crt-cc/lld-link Windows shared-build path already understands). (3) bignum.c's mbedtls_mpi_div_mpi() referencing undefined symbol __udivti3 (a compiler-rt/libgcc 128-bit-division intrinsic) -- this PAL's Windows sysroot has no compiler-rt/builtins archive at all (unlike Linux/macOS, where tools/crt-cc always links libclang_rt.builtins.a into every link, shared or not; Windows' own crt-cc libs list has no equivalent, a real, general gap worth a future dedicated fix, tracked informally here rather than in TODO.md since routing around it for mbedtls specifically was straightforward). Routed around for this port via -DMBEDTLS_HAVE_INT32 (forces bignum's portable 32-bit-limb path, no __int128 division), which conflicts with MBEDTLS_HAVE_ASM per bignum.h's own check_config.h -- so HAVE_ASM also needed disabling (Windows-only, CRT_TARGET_OS_WINDOWS-guarded patch; a plain -U on the CFLAGS was tried first and confirmed NOT to work, since mbedtls_config.h's own unguarded #define redefines it regardless of the command line). (4) Disabling HAVE_ASM then left MBEDTLS_AESNI_C unsatisfiable (library/aesni.h needs either HAVE_ASM or compiler intrinsics via -maes/-mpclmul, neither available) -- disabled too (Windows-only patch); no correctness loss, aes.c's portable table-based C implementation is used instead, confirmed correct by this port's own AES round-trip test. (5) A deeper, genuinely separate bug: mbedtls's top-level Makefile wraps its ENTIRE install:/uninstall: block in `ifndef WINDOWS` -- passing WINDOWS=1 (needed during the BUILD step to select the correctly-named .dll link recipes) to `make install` too doesn't just change install:'s behavior, it makes install: not exist at all (confirmed directly via GNU Make's own -p database dump: install: survives only as an empty .PHONY entry once WINDOWS=1 reaches it, so `make install WINDOWS=1` silently no-ops -- exit 0, nothing copied, no error -- which is how this went unnoticed for a full rebuild+test cycle before being caught by checking install output timestamps). Fixed generally, not with an mbedtls-specific hack: tools/crt-port-build.py gained a new target_overrides.<os>.build_make_args field, distinct from the existing (build+install)-shared target_overrides.<os>.make_args (kept as-is, since xz's own Windows recipe genuinely needs its override to reach both steps) -- build_make_args reaches ONLY the make_args build step, letting WINDOWS=1 move there and out of install_args.

porting/tests/mbedtls_crypto_test.c is a real cryptographic round trip, not a version-string/link-only smoke check: SHA-256("abc") compared against the actual NIST/FIPS 180-4 known-answer digest, plus a full AES-128-CBC encrypt/decrypt round trip verifying the decrypted output exactly reproduces the original plaintext (and that the ciphertext is not simply equal to the plaintext, so a no-op 'encrypt' couldn't accidentally pass). Verified natively first (WSL Ubuntu 20.04, plain gcc, against a native `make lib` + `make install DESTDIR=...` build) before wiring into this recipe/tools/crt-port-build.py at all.

Verified for real through this project's own toolchain end to end, BOTH static and shared, on Linux and Windows: `cmake --build --preset <preset> --target port-test-mbedtls` prints `mbedtls_crypto_test: ok sha256=ba7816bf8f01cfea... aes128cbc=roundtrip-ok` for both the crypto-static and crypto-shared test on Windows (real x86_64 host) and Linux (WSL Ubuntu 20.04 + clang-18, clean clone). Windows's shared test binary confirmed (via `llvm-objdump -p`) to genuinely dynamically depend on libmbedcrypto.dll, not accidentally statically linked. Also reran the full `port-test-recipes` aggregate on Windows (all recipes with automated tests, not just mbedtls) and the full Windows `ctest` suite (83/83) afterward to confirm the tools/crt-port-build.py changes (skip_configure, install_args, build_make_args) didn't regress any existing port or PAL test. Linux and Windows: shared-pass. macOS: untested (no local macOS hardware this session) -- APPLE_BUILD=1 is wired into target_overrides.macos.make_args (safe to reach both build and install, unlike Windows' WINDOWS=1, since APPLE_BUILD isn't involved in any ifndef gate around install: in the top-level Makefile) to select the correct DLEXT=dylib/.dylib link recipes, matching the same shared-build shape as Linux/Windows, but not yet run on real hardware.
